drawings.description: sous « $\operatorname{Spec} \mathbb{Z}$ », un trait horizontal portant un point marqué $x$ (la lettre au-dessous) ; un petit trait le coupe près de son extrémité droite.
drawings.kind: line with a marked point (Spec Z and a closed point x)
drawings.notes: A long horizontal stroke, slightly wavy on the page and drawn straight; a full point on it at about four tenths of its length, with the letter x just below; a short faint oblique tick across the stroke near its right end. Nothing struck. The note of the transcription does not mention the tick. Overlaid 2026-11-12 (Opus 5.5) on a 400 dpi colour render: the stroke, the point and the tick match the page; nothing corrected (on the colour scan the part of the stroke left of the point is brownish, the rest grey; drawn in one colour). Redrawn 2026-11-12 (issue 128): to check again.

drawings.description: schéma de la marge gauche ; au-dessous, un second schéma du même genre ($X_0$, $X$, $E$, $k_0$, $A_0$, $k$, $\mathbb{Q}$) est couvert de hachures et de traits, illisible
drawings.kind: two diagrams of fields and schemes (margin), the second hatched over
drawings.notes: Redrawn on a tight crop. Upper figure: X_0 - X over k_0 - A_0 - k with the two vertical strokes, the columns aligned (X_0 over A_0, X over k); the stroke k_0 - k is one stroke in the original with A_0 written on it, drawn as two pieces either side of the label. Lower figure (covered with hatching and loops): E - k_0 - A_0 on a heavy line, X_0 above with a vertical stroke through the line, a heavy stroke from X_0 up to the right, at the top right a dash and X with an arrow up from k (the arrowhead under X is a reading), below a heavy stroke from E down to A_0 and a heavy stroke from A_0 up to the right, a heavy stroke at the bottom; the hatched area over the right half is a hatched polygon, the long thin stroke from E to X and two of the loops at the bottom are drawn in pencil. Left out: a second X_0 scribbled over at the top of the hatched area, the remaining crossing strokes and loops. The Q of the transcription is not located with certainty (perhaps the loop at the bottom left, drawn as a loop without a label). Redrawn 2026-11-09 (issue 128): to check again. Question settled by a machine pass on the facsimile, 2026-11-12 (page and maths): the Q of the transcription is the looped letter at the bottom left of the second diagram, under k_0 and joined to it by a stroke (k_0 lies over Q, the foot of the tower); it is overwritten by the scribble. It is now drawn as the label Q in place of the unlabelled loop, with the stroke up to k_0 in pencil. Not checked by a reader. 2026-11-13, Claude Opus 5.5, overlay check (issue 147): not compiled (no TeX in the session); the TikZ rasterised and laid over the 350 dpi colour render of the scan. The upper diagram lies on the ink to within about 1 unit. The lower one is covered by a scribble of hatching and loops, which is a crossing-out: following the editor's rules (crossings-out are not figures; under a strike, what lies beneath is drawn), the hatched polygon and the large pencil ellipse that stood for the scribble are removed, and only what lies under it is kept (the labels E, k_0, A_0, X_0, X, k, Q, the heavy strokes, the arrow up to X, the thin stroke from E to X). Still differs, hence partial: under the scribble the lower diagram is illegible, as the transcription says; its heavy strokes are placed on their ink but what they join, and the second X_0 written over at the top of the scribble, cannot be read.
